answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall. A verifier challenges agents with a random memory path, creating a terrace of latency checks that filters out shared-cache entities. Within this kernel of logic, any agent failing to prove unique access to its physical bus is rejected as a stale relic of a pool. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, whereas fakes incur costs that scale linearly per identity, rendering pools inefficient by design.
